prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1405; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle sustained front-end damage. Claimant reports wrist injury and has retained counsel, who has requested all future communications be directed to their office. Scene photos and police report requested.

Entry 2: Received police report. Both vehicles were traveling at low speed when they made contact; no citations issued. Recorded statement taken from insured, who confirms the other vehicle crossed into the lane. Vehicle inspection scheduled with the appraiser.

Entry 3: Claimant's counsel submitted medical records indicating a fracture of the wrist treated with a splint and follow-up with an orthopedic specialist. Records reviewed and forwarded to the medical review unit. Bodily injury evaluation placed on hold pending receipt of complete treatment notes.

Entry 4: Appraiser report received. Repair estimate includes bumper, hood, radiator support, and headlamp assembly. Rental coverage confirmed for the insured. Counsel's office contacted to confirm the claimant's vehicle is a total loss candidate; valuation requested.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's counsel regarding outstanding wage loss documentation and final treatment summary. Counsel indicated a demand package will follow once the treating physician releases the claimant. File remains open; next review set for the upcoming diary date.
